findings.summary: record() retained caller's TraceEvent by reference — post-record mutation of filter/eventIds could silently rewrite trace history, threatening S3 classifier accuracy.
findings.fix: record() now JSON-clones the event before pushing into the buffer (TraceEvent is JSON-safe by construction: only string/number/string[]/plain-object filter, no functions, no cycles). Header comment block updated to document the contract.

findings.summary: dump() declared TraceEvent[] but no-op returned a frozen empty array cast back to mutable — production-only mutation trap.
findings.fix: Widened MlsTrace.dump() return type to `readonly TraceEvent[]`. Both no-op and recording impls return immutable views uniformly. Header comment updated.

findings.summary: No colocated test locked the contracts ahead of S2 wiring.
findings.fix: Added src/marmot/mls-trace.test.ts with 4 cases: clone-on-record (eventIds + groupId mutation), clone-on-record (nested filter mutation), dump-snapshot (mutating the dump array doesn't affect subsequent dumps), clear empties the buffer.

remediation_log.verdict: needs-attention (codex adversarial review last-mile, same round)

findings.summary: dump() leaked live event references in the recording impl — `buffer.slice()` is a shallow array copy; element refs were still shared with the buffer. A consumer could mutate a returned event's primitive field and rewrite the buffer in place.
findings.fix: Recording dump() now deep-clones each entry on egress: `buffer.map(e => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(e)) as TraceEvent)`. Symmetric with record(): together these close both leak directions (call-site → recorder, recorder → consumer). Header comment rewritten to document the symmetric clone contract.

findings.summary: Tests exercised an inline duplicate factory rather than the shipped implementation, so a regression in mls-trace.ts could leave the test suite green.
findings.fix: Exported `createRecordingTrace` as a named export from mls-trace.ts (with a JSDoc block explaining DCE remains intact: nothing else in the production graph references the export, so webpack DCEs it when NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_TRACE_MLS is unset). mls-trace.test.ts now imports the real factory. Added a 5th test case: dump-then-mutate-an-event regression test, asserting a subsequent dump still shows the original value.

notes: S1 ships src/marmot/mls-trace.ts and colocated src/marmot/mls-trace.test.ts. Module exports MlsTrace interface (record/dump/clear, dump returns `readonly TraceEvent[]`), TraceEvent discriminated union with all 20 variants from spec.md § Trace event shape, `createRecordingTrace` factory (named export so the test imports the shipped factory), and a `mlsTrace` const + default export. Recording-vs-no-op selection happens once at module load via `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_TRACE_MLS === "1"` so production webpack DCE removes the recording branch and the unused `createRecordingTrace` export. record() and dump() are SYMMETRIC ABOUT JSON-CLONING: record() clones on enqueue (call-site → recorder leak closed), dump() clones each entry on egress (recorder → consumer leak closed). Pure module — only `import type { Filter }` from applesauce-core, no react/next/DOM. Adjacent cleanup: 2 pre-existing TS implicit-any errors in e2e/tests/viewport-audit.spec.ts (lines 21, 26) typed explicitly to clear the tsc gate (boy-scout rule). Both `make test` (12 files / 84 tests, +1 file / +5 tests vs baseline) and `npx tsc --noEmit` are green. No call sites yet — those land in S2.
